papers.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
papers.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysoz
papers.summary: This study performed deep longitudinal metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from a single individual over 3.6 years (51 time points), capturing gut microbiome dynamics during episodes of severe colonic inflammation. Using time-point-specific genome-scale metabolic models and flux balance analysis, the authors predicted microbial metabolic phenotypes and compared them with clinical inflammation biomarkers such as CRP, lactoferrin, and calprotectin. The work demonstrates that dense single-subject sampling combined with metabolic modeling can link microbiome composition and predicted metabolic flux to host inflammatory status.

papers.title: An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To characterize systemic transcriptomic signatures and identify candidate hub genes associated with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) in peripheral blood using an integrative systems-biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies an integrative systems-biology approach to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene-expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets for LSCC. The work highlights the value of combining transcriptomics with network analysis to detect non-tissue-based signals of cancer.

papers.title: Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.
papers.abstract: The distinction between primary and secondary metabolism has long provided a useful conceptual and pedagogical framework in biochemistry, particularly in plant sciences, but it increasingly fails as a literal description of how metabolites are produced and function. Pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulatory mechanisms, transport systems, and recycling routes, while metabolites conventionally assigned to different categories can contribute to growth, signaling, defense, nutrient acquisition, structure, or stress responses depending on context. Here, we review the historical origins of th
papers.summary: This review argues that the traditional division between primary and secondary metabolism in plants is conceptually outdated. The authors show that metabolic pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulation, transport, and recycling, and that metabolites can serve growth, signaling, defense, or stress roles depending on context. They call for a unified metabolic perspective that better reflects how metabolites are actually produced and function.

papers.title: M-SCAN: Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks for Genome-Scale Flux Inference in Pan-Cancer Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism reflects both recurrent tumour programmes and tissue-specific constraints, but transcriptome analyses do not directly estimate metabolic reaction fluxes. We developed Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks (M-SCAN), a reproducible workflow for sample-wise genome-scale flux inference across heterogeneous cancer cohorts.
papers.summary: M-SCAN is a reproducible workflow that infers genome-scale metabolic reaction fluxes for individual tumor samples across heterogeneous pan-cancer cohorts, addressing the gap that transcriptome data alone cannot directly estimate metabolic flux. It combines multi-scale constraint-based modeling to capture both recurrent tumor metabolic programs and tissue-specific constraints.

papers.title: Protocol for thermodynamic analysis of genome-scale metabolic models using dGbyG and ThermoInfer.
papers.abstract: Accurate thermodynamic information can be used to improve the quality of genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs). Here, we present a computational protocol that integrates the dGbyG and ThermoInfer algorithms for thermodynamic analysis of GEMs. We describe steps for setting up the computational environment, implementing a workflow for predicting standard Gibbs free energy changes using dGbyG, and performing thermodynamic flux balance analysis with ThermoInfer to identify thermodynamically inconsistent reactions. We illustrate the workflow using the Yeast9-GEM model as an example. For complete det
papers.summary: This protocol describes how to combine two computational tools, dGbyG and ThermoInfer, to add thermodynamic constraints to genome-scale metabolic models. dGbyG predicts standard Gibbs free energy changes for reactions, and ThermoInfer uses these to perform thermodynamic flux balance analysis and flag thermodynamically inconsistent reactions. The workflow is demonstrated on the Yeast9-GEM model.

papers.title: The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.
papers.abstract: Chronic degenerative diseases are traditionally explained in terms of disease-specific initiating lesions and molecular pathways. Although this approach has substantially advanced understanding of disease mechanisms, it does not fully explain why biologically diverse disorders often converge on persistent states marked by chronic inflammation, impaired repair, altered nutrient sensing, reduced adaptive flexibility, and incomplete recovery after the initiating insult subsides. This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS), a systems-level framework that distinguishes disease init
papers.summary: This perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS) as a systems-level framework to explain why biologically diverse chronic diseases converge on persistent states of chronic inflammation, impaired repair, and reduced adaptive flexibility even after the initiating insult resolves. It argues that disease-specific lesion models are insufficient and that a shared systems-level state underlies chronic disease persistence.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: Researchers built the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, using a new nutrient-controlled reconstruction approach. They also established comprehensive nutrient requirements for controlled in vitro growth and analyzed the bacterium's secretions. This provides a more accurate computational tool for studying LGG metabolism in industrial and health contexts.

papers.title: Meta-finetuning foundation models for generalizable biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes.
papers.abstract: Biological image segmentation is essential for analyzing cellular structures, yet labeled data are often labor-intensive and expensive to obtain, which limits conventional deep learning models in low-data settings. Building upon the bi-level meta-finetuning formulation introduced in BLO-SAM, we evaluate MetaTune for adapting foundation models to biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes. MetaTune separates the model's learnable components into meta-parameters, which enhance generalization, and non-meta parameters, which focus on task-specific adaptation. Through an iterative, two
papers.summary: MetaTune adapts foundation models for biological image segmentation when labeled data are extremely scarce, by splitting the model's parameters into meta-parameters that promote generalization and non-meta parameters that handle task-specific adaptation. Building on the BLO-SAM bi-level meta-finetuning formulation, it shows that this separation improves segmentation performance in ultra-low-data regimes where conventional deep learning struggles.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and, importantly, for evaluating how well the inferred network structure captures causal gene-gene relationships. This addresses a gap in widely available software for both Bayesian network inference and structural/causal accuracy assessment in single-cell GRN analysis.

papers.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
papers.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This review discusses how computational (in-silico) methods can be integrated with traditional ethnopharmacological knowledge to accelerate herbal drug discovery. It argues that combining traditional disease classification with modern computational tools can help identify bioactive phytochemicals and clarify their mechanisms of action, addressing a key barrier to clinical translation.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections from spatial omics experiments using only their associated microscopy images, without requiring shared molecular features or manual annotations. It enables construction of unified multi-modal molecular datasets and performs comparably to established uni-modal alignment tools across different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions.

papers.title: Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information.
papers.summary: This paper compares interventional causal structure learning algorithms for inferring gene regulatory networks, evaluating how well different methods recover causal structure when intervention data are available. It provides a practical assessment of which algorithms perform best under realistic conditions, helping guide method choice for GRN inference.

papers.title: Dolphin semen metabolome characterization and relationships with sperm quality.
papers.abstract: Identification and quantification of metabolites in semen can augment assisted reproductive technologies by indicating reproductive health and fertility. Species-specific semen metabolites associated with improved semen quality remain largely unknown in exotic species due to limited sample availability.
papers.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
papers.summary: This study characterizes the metabolome of dolphin semen and examines associations between specific metabolites and sperm quality parameters. By identifying species-specific seminal metabolites linked to improved semen quality, the work aims to support assisted reproductive technologies for this exotic species despite limited sample availability.

papers.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a su
papers.summary: The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. These models quantified how BRCA1 loss rewires metabolic pathways and identified 28 enzyme-level metabolic vulnerabilities, 24 of which map to existing or approved drugs. Independent DepMap data supported the predictions, suggesting a framework for prioritizing metabolic drug targets in BRCA1-deficient cancers.

papers.title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.
papers.abstract: Gravitropism redirects plant organ growth by converting gravity perception into asymmetric growth initiated in endodermal statocytes. Although the C2H2-type zinc finger transcription factor SHOOT GRAVITROPISM 5 (SGR5), also known as INDETERMINATE DOMAIN 15 (IDD15), is essential for shoot gravitropism, the transcriptional mechanisms linking gravity perception to directional growth remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing to build a transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis stem during gravitropism, focusing on the endodermal cells that sense gravity. It identifies the gene regulatory network downstream of the transcription factor SGR5/IDD15, clarifying how gravity perception is converted into asymmetric growth. The atlas provides a cell-type-resolved resource for understanding plant gravitropic signaling.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in data integration: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.
papers.abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of
papers.summary: This paper proposes 'Longevitomics' as a new integrative systems framework for studying healthy longevity, defining the 'Longevitome' as the dynamic multi-layered architecture of molecular, microbiome, digital phenotyping, and AI-derived data that together determine long life. Rather than studying each omics layer or biomarker in isolation, the framework argues for unifying genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, and digital phenotyping into a single predictive systems model of healthy aging.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira grown at host-like 37°C upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that this pathogen relies mainly on fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Network inference at single-cell resolution reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in limb evolution.
papers.abstract: How changes in conserved developmental genetic programs contribute to morphological evolution remains poorly understood, particularly in non-conventional model species. Here, we combine single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility profiling with cross-species label transfer and gene regulatory network inference to compare mouse and pig limb development. Our analyses identify broadly conserved cellular organization but discrete divergence in HOX-, FGF- and SHH-regulated programs. FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds phenocopies the distal expansion of pig GREM1 expression, while altered
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares limb development between mice and pigs using single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility, combined with gene regulatory network inference and cross-species label transfer. The authors find that overall cellular organization is conserved but that specific HOX-, FGF-, and SHH-regulated programs diverge between species. Pharmacological FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds recapitulates the distal expansion of GREM1 expression seen in pigs, suggesting that network rewiring and buffering mechanisms underlie morphological evolution.

papers.title: Stochasticity in Metabolism: Oxidative Stress Response Phenotypes As Emergent Consequences of Network Topology.
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. Traditional ROS modeling has been confined to small ODE frameworks limited by kinetic-parameter scarcity. Here, we recast ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis (FBA) optimization problem using COBRA and CPLEX, augmenting the Escherichia coli iJO1366 genome-scale model with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions, targeting three ROS species: hydroxyl radicals, superoxide, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). We also fo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors extend the E. coli genome-scale metabolic model iJO1366 with reactions for ROS production, redox, and detoxification, and reformulate ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis optimization problem. This enables genome-scale simulation of oxidative stress response phenotypes, which they argue emerge from network topology and stochasticity rather than from detailed kinetic parameters.

papers.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
papers.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from lab to field scale for soil bioremediation, integrating mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives. It identifies key barriers limiting field performance and proposes evidence-based design principles for engineering plant-microbe-soil consortia. The work is a synthesis rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.
papers.summary: scPhyloGRN is a new method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by using the lineage tree (phylogeny) of cells to guide regulatory inference, separating expression variation due to shared ancestry from that due to cell state. This addresses a key confounder in GRN inference, where related cells share expression patterns that can be mistaken for regulatory relationships.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.
papers.summary: This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging cochlea, tracking how different cell types change over time. It identifies two distinct phases of age-related inflammation (biphasic inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network reconstruction, and bulk validation across cohorts.

papers.title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. Strain-specific GSMMs clustered by clonal complex (CC): in all nine CCs with ≥ 2 isolates the mean within-CC Jaccard distance was smaller than the mean between-CC distance; across all strain pairs the med
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed genome-scale metabolic models for 86 Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates and found that the models cluster by clonal complex, with within-lineage metabolic similarity consistently exceeding between-lineage similarity. They validated this structure against in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. The work shows that lineage-level metabolic structure is detectable from genomic data alone and provides a resource of strain-specific models for this pathogen.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 correlate with semen quality in rams, using ejaculates from five animals assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis. The authors found that protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility and used gene regulatory network analysis to propose upstream regulators. The work extends protamine biology from well-studied species into ram reproduction and suggests these genes as candidate markers of male fertility.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, this score-level meta-classifier offers a way to resolve disagreements between inference methods instead of choosing one or averaging all.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors produce a high-quality genome annotation (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and identify 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEAs, revealing their coordinated transcriptional regulation. The work provides a resource for understanding salt tolerance mechanisms in halophytes.

papers.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell multiomics data to map the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis, identifying cellular and molecular changes underlying disease pathogenesis. It provides a detailed view of how epithelial and stromal cells communicate in the allergic nasal mucosa, potentially revealing new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using a computational genome-scale metabolic model tailored to endothelial cells, the authors predicted and experimentally validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization during angiogenesis. This previously overlooked transporter supports endothelial biomass synthesis and proliferation, linking glutamine metabolism to new blood vessel formation.

papers.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
papers.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi
papers.summary: Researchers built the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for Xylella fastidiosa, the bacterium causing devastating crop diseases, by integrating conserved metabolic functions across 18 strains from five subspecies. The manually curated consensus model, iXfcore, captures core metabolic capabilities and enables simulation of the pathogen's metabolism despite its fastidious growth. This provides a foundation for studying X. fastidiosa biology and potentially identifying metabolic vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode
papers.summary: This study combines a genome-scale metabolic model of Rhodopseudomonas palustris with machine learning to explore the design space for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production. The hybrid framework identifies cost-efficient strategies for boosting PHB yields, addressing the high substrate and operational costs that limit microbial bioplastic production. It demonstrates how computational optimization can guide strain and process design without exhaustive experimental screening.

papers.title: A pathogen-free citrus model recapitulates Huanglongbing-associated molecular and physiological reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a devastating citrus disease associated with "Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus", but the contribution of host-driven processes to disease development remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a pathogen-free system to determine whether chloroplast dysfunction can reproduce key molecular and physiological features of HLB. Using Citrus tristeza virus-mediated silencing of phytoene desaturase (PDS) and δ-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALAD), we simultaneously disrupted carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis in Citrus macrophylla. Chloroplast dysfunction induced foli
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: The authors created a pathogen-free citrus model by using virus-induced gene silencing to knock down two chloroplast biosynthesis genes (PDS and ALAD) in Citrus macrophylla, simultaneously disrupting carotenoid and chlorophyll production. This chloroplast dysfunction reproduced key molecular and physiological features of Huanglongbing (HLB), suggesting that host chloroplast breakdown—rather than the pathogen itself—drives much of the disease phenotype. The work provides a tractable system for studying HLB mechanisms without needing the unculturable pathogen.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.
papers.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold tremendous promise for disease modeling, drug discovery, and cardiac regenerative therapies. However, the immature phenotype of hPSC-CMs remains a major barrier limiting their translational utility. Here, we performed integrated multi-omic profiling to identify molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with hPSC-CM maturation during long-term culture. hPSC-CMs were cultured for 113 days and analyzed using metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics across progressive stages of maturation. Long-term culture induced
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes over 113 days of culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs that drive maturation. The multi-omic approach reveals progressive maturation programs that could help overcome the immature phenotype limiting translational use of these cells.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review argues that TREM2 acts as a central molecular hub governing macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the simple M1/M2 classification. It emphasizes that the timing of TREM2 signaling and the diversity of macrophage states shape disease progression, and it highlights TREM2 as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This paper argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms. The work serves as a methodological guide for toxicologists seeking rigorous causal inference in systems-level biology.

papers.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors found that metabolic features of pediatric environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) overlap with maternal plasma proteomic signatures linked to fetal growth restriction, suggesting that some of the EED metabolic signature may originate before birth rather than being purely acquired intestinal pathology. The analysis drew on duodenal transcriptomics from 52 children with EED and 24 controls in the SEEM cohort and was validated across two independent cohorts.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Machine Learning Reveal Oxidative Stress Hubs and Therapeutic Targets in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that oxidative stress is involved in its pathophysiology. This study explored oxidative stress-related mechanisms in IBS-D and screened potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrative bioinformatics analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics and machine learning to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes and candidate biomarkers in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D). The authors propose oxidative stress hubs as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets, though the findings are based on computational analysis of existing datasets.

papers.title: BoolFunc-EA: A Boolean-evolutionary approach for accurate inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Network inference is the process of discovering genetic information from time-series data. The inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series data represents a significant challenge in bioinformatics. Despite the development of many Boolean network inference methods, most struggle with scalability as they impose restrictions on regulatory genes for each target gene. Other methods suffer from local optimum issues or are unable to compute the exact mutual information between a regulatory gene and its target gene. To resolve these issues, we present a novel method referred to as BoolFunc-
papers.summary: The paper introduces BoolFunc-EA, a Boolean network inference method that combines evolutionary algorithms with Boolean function learning to reconstruct gene regulatory networks from time-series expression data. It aims to overcome scalability limits, local optima, and inaccurate mutual information estimates that affect existing Boolean network inference approaches. The method is presented as a more accurate alternative for inferring regulatory relationships from temporal gene expression measurements.

papers.title: Transcriptome-Based, Genome-Scale Metabolic Modeling of Haemonchus contortus during Development and between Sexes.
papers.abstract: Parasitic nematodes undergo developmental transitions between external and host-associated environments, yet the accompanying changes in metabolic capacity remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed HaeconGEM, a genome-scale metabolic model of the blood-feeding nematode Haemonchus contortus. HaeconGEM v1 comprises 1,420 genes and 11,873 reactions. We integrated transcriptomic data from the egg, the L1 to L3 larval stages, female and male L4 larvae, and adult females and males to generate 8 transcriptome-constrained models. papers.summary: The authors built HaeconGEM, a genome-scale metabolic model for the parasitic nematode Haemonchus contortus, containing 1,420 genes and 11,873 reactions. By integrating transcriptomic data from eggs, larval stages, and adult males and females, they generated eight stage- and sex-specific models that reveal how metabolic capacity shifts across development and between sexes. This provides a computational framework for understanding parasite metabolism and identifying potential drug targets.

papers.title: A deep network embedding and robust statistical framework for multi-omics integration in rare diseases: a case study in PMM2-CDG.
papers.abstract: Integrative analysis of multiomic datasets in rare diseases is often constrained by small-n cohorts, impeding the identification of robust and biologically meaningful disease mechanisms. We developed an end-to-end framework that combines multiomic integration, robust statistical inference and network representation learning to extract clinically relevant molecular signatures from limited sample sizes. The framework prioritizes informative omic layers using Multiple Factor Analysis, identifies stable severity-associated features through stability selection and projects these features onto the h
papers.summary: The authors present an end-to-end computational framework that integrates multiple omics layers from small rare-disease cohorts using Multiple Factor Analysis, stability selection, and deep network embedding, applied to PMM2-CDG. The approach prioritizes informative omic layers and identifies stable severity-associated molecular features despite limited sample sizes, then projects them onto a network representation for biological interpretation.

papers.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the cellular heterogeneity of the ovarian ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), arguing that the disorder's clinical variability stems from diverse cell types and their interactions rather than a single pathway. It integrates endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory evidence to propose a more unified, cell-resolved framework for understanding PCOS.
